$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.oracle. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-ORACLE-FIRST-CONFIGURATION-IS-ENOUGH
arms.find: final asked: Array<OracleConfig> = cut < 0 ? oracles : oracles.slice(0, cut + 1);
arms.note: only the FIRST configuration is ever asked, so an edit that compiles under one set of defines and breaks another is applied - the cross-configuration hole the list exists to close

arms.name: M-ORACLE-RED-BASELINE-STOPS-THE-PHASE
arms.note: any configuration red before the run stops the whole phase again, so one broken target leaves every risky fix report-only - including in files that target never reads and a green configuration verifies

arms.name: M-ORACLE-COVERAGE-PAIRED-BY-INDEX
arms.replace: return [for (i in 0...oracles.length) i < memo.probes.length ? memo.probes[i].coverage : probedFor(memo, oracles[i])];
arms.note: a seeded probe is handed to whichever configuration sits at its position, so a phase judging a different subset reads another build's compiled set and verifies an edit the judging build never compiles

arms.name: M-ORACLE-UNKNOWN-COVERAGE-STOPS-THE-PHASE
arms.note: one configuration whose compiled set is unknown stops the whole phase again, so its known siblings judge nothing - the policy a red baseline no longer follows

arms.name: M-GENERATE-NEVER-STALE-BY-INPUT
arms.find: for (input in inputs) if (hashIn(recordedInputs, input) != hashOf(input, memo)) return '$input changed';
arms.note: a changed generateInputs file no longer makes the recorded generation stale, so an hxml generated from an older project.xml keeps answering for a build that no longer exists

arms.name: M-GENERATE-NEVER-STALE-BY-COMMAND
arms.find: if (record.command != group.generate.command) return 'its generate command changed';
arms.note: a changed generate command no longer regenerates, so an entry whose recipe was edited keeps the hxml the old recipe wrote

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TRUSTS-A-MISSING-HXML
find: for (hxml in group.hxmls) if (!sys.FileSystem.exists(hxml)) return '$hxml is missing';
for (hxml in group.hxmls) if (hashIn(recordedOutputs, hxml) != hashOf(hxml, memo)) return '$hxml changed since it was generated';
arms.note: an hxml deleted or edited after its generation was recorded is read as current, so the configuration compiles a missing or hand-edited file

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FAILURE-USES-THE-STALE-HXML
arms.note: a failed generate command no longer makes its configuration unavailable, so the hxml an earlier generation left behind silently answers for the build

arms.name: M-SPAWN-RUN-IGNORES-CWD
arms.note: a single haxe spawn runs in the process cwd whatever the configuration's dir says, so a relative -cp resolves against the wrong tree and the typecheck and every probe answer about a different project

arms.name: M-SPAWN-RUNALL-IGNORES-CWD
arms.find: const opts = { cwd: j.cwd == null ? undefined : j.cwd,
arms.note: the parallel driver spawns every job in its own cwd rather than the job's, so overlapped typechecks and coverage probes of a configuration with a dir answer about a different tree

arms.name: M-DRIVER-CANCELS-EARLIER-JOBS
arms.find: for (let k = i + 1; k < jobs.length; k++)
arms.note: a failing job also kills the jobs declared BEFORE it, so the overlapped verdict is the first failure to finish rather than the first in declared order

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-IGNORES-DIR
arms.note: the verdict fingerprint resolves the hxml's classpath against the process cwd, so an edit under the configuration's dir leaves a stored verdict matching

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-IGNORES-DIR
arms.note: the display server is warmed and queried from the process cwd, so a configuration with a dir never warms and the oracle-assisted phase is skipped

arms.name: M-GENERATE-HASHES-INPUTS-AFTER-THE-RUN
arms.note: the explicit inputs are hashed after the command instead of before, so an edit landing during a generation is recorded beside an hxml built from the old content and never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RECORD-OUTLIVES-THE-RUN
arms.note: the previous generation's record survives while a stale command runs, so a generation killed half way leaves a partial tree that reads as current forever

arms.name: M-GENERATE-DIRECTORY-INPUT-CONSTANT
arms.note: a directory input hashes to one constant, so a file added or edited under it never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FIRST-ENTRY-INPUTS
arms.find: held.inputs = mine == null || theirs == null ? null : theirs.concat([for (input in mine) if (!theirs.contains(input)) input]);
arms.note: entries sharing one command keep only the first entry's inputs, so a change to an input only a later entry declares never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-LOCK-IGNORED
arms.note: every lock holder reads as dead, so a live run's exclusive hold is taken over and its tree regenerated under it

arms.name: M-GENERATE-LOCK-NEVER-RECOVERED
arms.note: a lock left by a dead run is waited for as if its owner lived, so one crashed run makes every later one unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-EMPTY-INPUTS-NEVER
arms.note: an empty generateInputs list is kept, so the entry never regenerates while an absent list regenerates every run

arms.name: M-GENERATE-MISSING-INPUT-SILENT
arms.find: drops.push('compilerOracle[$index] "generateInputs" names $input, which does not exist — kept, it counts once created');
arms.note: a generateInputs path that does not exist is accepted silently, so a typo makes that input a constant nobody hears about

arms.name: M-DRIVER-NEVER-STOPS
arms.note: a failing job no longer ends the later ones, so a rejection waits for and pays every compile declared after it

arms.name: M-DRIVER-KILLS-ONLY-THE-SHELL
arms.note: a kill reaches only the shell, so a build tool it started keeps writing into the generated tree after its job was cancelled

arms.name: M-DRIVER-NO-TIMEOUT
arms.find: if (j.timeout > 0) c.timer = setTimeout(() => { c.timedOut = true; kill(c); }, j.timeout);
arms.note: a job's timeout is ignored, so a hung generate command blocks the run forever

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-STORES-A-MOVED-FINGERPRINT
arms.note: a verdict is filed under the pre-compile fingerprint even when the tree moved during the compile, so a verdict about a half-regenerated tree is handed to the next run of the complete one

arms.name: M-GENERATE-IGNORES-LIBRARY-STATE
arms.note: the library state the generated hxml names is not an input, so a haxelib version or dev-path switch leaves an hxml naming the old library paths current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-READERS-EXCLUDE-EACH-OTHER
arms.note: every run takes every generation exclusively, so one agent's long --fix run blocks every other lint over a tree nobody regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-WRITER-IGNORES-READERS
arms.note: a regeneration no longer waits for the runs still compiling the old tree, so its rm -rf lands under their typecheck

arms.name: M-GENERATE-OWNERLESS-ABANDONED-AT-ONCE
arms.note: a writer caught between its mkdir and its owner write is taken over at once, so two runs both hold the lock

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TAKEOVER-UNVERIFIED
arms.find: final same: Bool = current != null && current.identity == stale.identity;
arms.note: a run that judged an owner dead too late removes the fresh writer that replaced it, so two runs both win the takeover

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PID-ALONE
arms.note: a lock owner is judged by its pid alone, so a pid the system reused keeps a dead run's lock for hours

arms.name: M-DRIVER-SIGNAL-ORPHANS
arms.note: a signalled driver exits without its detached job groups, so Ctrl-C leaves a build tool writing into dist/oracle

arms.name: M-GENERATE-REPO-DIR-FROM-NAME
arms.note: a dev install is not traced to the repository directory whose .dev points at it, so haxelib dev on a library whose json name differs from its directory never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-IMPLICIT-HASHED-AFTER-THE-RUN
arms.note: implicit inputs are hashed only after the command, so a library switched while it ran is recorded as the state the hxml was built against

arms.name: M-GENERATE-HASH-MEMO-UNUSED
arms.note: every generation naming a path reads and hashes it again, so a large shared input such as fonts/ is read once per build per run

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TEMPLATES-UNTRACKED
arms.note: a library's code templates are not inputs, so a changed lime ApplicationMain template leaves the generated sources stale

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-MEMO-UNREAD
arms.note: the fingerprint memo is never read, so every configuration re-reads and re-hashes the whole source tree before and after the compiles

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PRODUCED-INCLUDE-IS-INPUT
arms.note: an hxml the generation writes and includes is compared across the run as if it were an input, so every generation that rewrites it goes unrecorded and regenerates forever (lime's iOS Build.hxml)

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARED-HELD-INTO-PHASE-TWO
arms.note: a run keeps its shared holds while it waits for exclusive ones, so two runs that each find two generations stale wait for each other until the deadline and each loses a configuration

arms.name: M-GENERATE-CLAIM-NEVER-CLEARED
arms.note: a takeover claim left by a run that died mid-takeover is never cleared, so every later run waits on a writer nobody can take over

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TAKEOVER-LEAVES-THE-JOB
arms.note: a takeover removes the dead run's writer while its generate job still runs, so that build tool writes on into a tree the next generation owns

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FORMAT-UNCHECKED
arms.find: if (record.format != FORMAT_TAG) return 'its generation was recorded by an older engine';
arms.note: a record written under an older scheme is trusted, so records whose implicit inputs an older engine derived differently keep answering as current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PRODUCED-BY-ROOT
arms.note: any include under a wider tree than the hxml's own output directory counts as produced, so an edited project hxml the generated one includes goes unnoticed during a generation

arms.name: M-DRIVER-OUTLIVES-ITS-PARENT
arms.note: a driver whose apq was SIGKILLed keeps its jobs running, so the next run regenerates concurrently with an orphaned build tool

arms.name: M-DRIVER-KILLS-WITHOUT-GRACE
arms.note: a killed job gets a bare SIGKILL again, so a pool lease wrapper cannot forward its end and the command it runs in a group of its own outlives the run with its threads

arms.name: M-DRIVER-NO-HARD-KILL
arms.note: a job group that ignores the SIGTERM is never SIGKILLed after the grace, so a stubborn tool keeps running until the driver's last-resort exit or forever

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARE-WITHOUT-REJUDGE
arms.note: a group judged current before another run wiped it is shared for the compile without being judged again, so a half-written tree is typechecked and vetoes an edit falsely

arms.name: M-GENERATE-REJUDGE-UNBOUNDED
arms.find: refuse(run, group, 'it went stale again $attempts time(s) while this run waited — another run keeps moving it');
arms.note: a group still stale after the bounded retries is handed to the compile anyway instead of being made unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-IN-TMPDIR
arms.note: the generation record and lock live under TMPDIR, so runs with different TMPDIRs share no lock and rm -rf the same tree concurrently

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-DIR-HASHED
arms.note: a directory input that holds the generation root hashes hxq's own state, which every generation rewrites, so it never reads as current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-NOT-IGNORED
arms.note: the state directory's .gitignore matches nothing, so every project has to list .apq/ in its own ignore file again

arms.name: M-GENERATE-IGNORE-OVERWRITTEN
arms.note: an ignore file already inside the state directory is rewritten on every run, discarding whatever the project put there

arms.name: M-GENERATE-ORDER-BY-KEY
arms.note: waits follow the declaration key rather than the lock identity, so two runs declaring one tree under different commands can take its locks in opposite orders

arms.name: M-GENERATE-ENDJOB-PID-ONLY
arms.note: a left job with no recorded start time is killed on its pid alone, which may name an unrelated process group by now

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARE-JUDGES-STALENESS
arms.note: the compile hold asks whether a group is current instead of whether it moved since this run looked, so an entry with no inputs, or one whose command writes its own input, is regenerated until it is given up on

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-COMMAND-RETRIED
arms.note: a tree another configuration regenerated with a different command is sent back through regeneration, so two configurations take it back and forth instead of one being told why it is unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-COMMANDS-KEPT
arms.note: an hxml two different generate commands of one config claim is kept, so both commands run into one tree and one configuration is always unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-READ-ONLY-ROOT-THROWS
arms.find:
catch (exception: Exception) 'cannot create its generation state under ${Path.directory(Path.directory(stateDir(group)))}: '
			+ exception.message;
arms.note: a generation root where the state cannot be created crashes the run instead of making its configurations unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-BY-CONFIG-ROOT
arms.note: the generation state lives beside the declaring config, so two configs over one tree take two locks and delete the tree under each other

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: the generation state is keyed by the hxml as spelled, so a symlinked spelling of one tree takes a second lock

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-IN-OUTPUT-DIR
arms.note: a project marker in the hxml's own directory puts the generation state inside the tree the command may delete

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-ROOT-FROM-HXML
arms.note: the project root is searched from above the hxml, so a marker the generation writes at its output root holds the state it deletes, and a top-level hxml climbs into an enclosing repository

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: two spellings of one hxml under two commands are not seen as rivals, so both commands run into one tree

arms.name: M-GENERATE-EPOCH-UNOBSERVED
arms.note: another run's generation that left the record and hxml as they were goes unseen, though it rewrote the rest of the tree

arms.name: M-DEFINES-ONE-ARM
arms.find: if (arms != 1 || early == null || all == null) return null;
arms.replace: if (early == null || all == null) return null;
arms.note: a transcript of several compile arms is read as the last arm's alone

arms.name: M-DEFINES-EARLY
arms.note: a define an initialization macro sets is read as defined for every file, so a module an earlier one typed is judged under it

arms.name: M-DEFINES-TYPES
arms.note: the probe names no type the build typed, so a type a macro defined reads as held by the index

arms.name: M-DEFINES-IMPL
arms.note: (precision) an abstract's implementation class is reported, which no source declares, so every build with an abstract reads as incomplete

arms.name: M-SPAWN-ORDER
arms.find: if (answer != null && answer.length == jobs.length) return answer;
arms.replace: if (answer != null && answer.length == jobs.length) return [for (k in 0...answer.length) answer[answer.length - 1 - k]];
arms.note: overlapping compiles answer in the order they finished, so one configuration's defines decide another's branches

arms.name: M-ORACLE-PARALLEL-HALF-THE-CORES
arms.note: the compile budget is half the cores again, so a thirteen-configuration project compiles in four waves on a sixteen-core machine

arms.name: M-ORACLE-PARALLEL-COUNTS-SLOW-CORES
arms.note: the efficiency cores count as compile threads again, so every round waits on the compiles that landed on the slowest cores

arms.name: M-ORACLE-PARALLEL-IGNORES-LEASE
arms.note: a run under a pool lease takes the whole machine again, so its compiles crowd out the processes the lease was shared with

arms.name: M-POOL-SERVERS-NEED-PARALLELISM
arms.note: a compile budget smaller than the configurations starts no warm server at all, so every typecheck of a fix run compiles cold

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-PROBE-RECOMPILES
arms.find: final held: Array<Null<HaxeRun>> = [for (i in 0...asked.length) memo?.run(asked[i], true, before[i])];
arms.note: the coverage probe compiles the tree its baseline just compiled with -v, paying a second compile per configuration

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-KEY-IGNORES-CONTENT
arms.note: a remembered verdict answers for any content of the tree, so an edit that breaks the build is judged by the verdict of the tree before it

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-QUOTES-THE-VERBOSE-STREAMS
arms.find: for (k in 0...runs.length) if (answered(runs[k]) && runs[k].status != 0 && decided(runs[k], decisive) == null) k
arms.note: a failing -v baseline is quoted with its -v lines, so a rejection's text names every parsed file

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-FILES-A-MOVED-INPUT
arms.note: a compile whose input changed while it ran is filed under the content it started from, so that content is later answered with a verdict about another

arms.name: M-PENDING-RUNS-IN-FOREGROUND
arms.find: final answer: Array<HaxeRun> = pid == null ? HaxeSpawn.runAll(_jobs, _maxBuffer, _parallel, false, _bound) : collect(pid);
arms.note: a background batch is run again in the foreground when it is awaited, so nothing it did while the caller worked is saved

arms.name: M-PENDING-CANCEL-LEAVES-JOBS
arms.note: a cancelled batch leaves its driver running, so the jobs it started run to their end after the run abandoned them

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-WRITTEN-UNHASHED
arms.note: the run's fingerprint rests on the library directories hashed earlier in the process, so an edit to a project whose sources arrive through -lib leaves it unchanged and the verification is answered from the baseline

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-TRUSTS-UNSEEN-SOURCES
arms.note: a configuration that reads files outside every directory its fingerprint walks is answered from the memo, so an edit there reuses a verdict about the old content

arms.name: M-PENDING-JOBS-FILE-KEPT
arms.note: the driver leaves the job list in its directory, so a run killed mid-batch leaves the job list behind

arms.name: M-DEFINES-VALUES-STABLE
arms.find: if (value != null && finalValues[d] == value) values[d] = value;
arms.note: a value an initialization macro changed after the first one saw it is read as the value every file saw

arms.name: M-DEFINES-VALUES-MACRO
arms.note: the probe prints no value at the first initialization macro, so no define has one

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-WALK-FIRST-ONLY
arms.note: a run's shared walk reads only the first directory it is asked for, so a classpath outside the compile root drops out of every later configuration's fingerprint and an edit there is answered from the memo

arms.name: M-POOL-NO-INVALIDATE
arms.note: the pool tells a server nothing moved, so a text the run rewrote within the second the server last compiled is answered as it was

arms.name: M-POOL-TRUSTS-WARM-RED
arms.note: a warm rejection is the verdict, so a server re-emitting a stale diagnostic reverts a sound fix

arms.name: M-TETHER-IGNORES-EOF
arms.find: process.stdin.on("end", end); process.stdin.on("close", end); process.stdin.on("error", end); process.stdin.resume();
arms.note: a tether never reads its stdin, so the driver's death goes unnoticed and a tethered server outlives the run

arms.name: M-POOL-SERVER-UNTETHERED
arms.note: the run's warm servers are plain jobs of their own process groups, so a SIGKILL of the group apq and the driver share leaves each one running with no owner

arms.name: M-POOL-NEVER-RESTARTS
arms.note: a server whose tree moved by more paths than invalidating them is worth is invalidated path by path, one walk of its whole cache each, instead of being replaced by a fresh server

arms.name: M-POOL-INVALIDATION-REACHES-EVERYTHING
arms.note: a file that appeared or vanished, or one that is no module, is only invalidated by its own path, which reaches no module that depends on it, so a server keeps answering green over an ambient import file or a macro-read file it never saw change

arms.name: M-POOL-REREAD-COUNTS-AS-APPEARED
arms.note: the module a position request dropped from the server's record counts as a file that appeared, so every compile after a position round replaces the server by a fresh one that compiles cold

arms.name: M-POOL-END-CANCELS-ALL
arms.note: the pool's servers share one fate again: giving up one configuration's server ends every other server with it

arms.name: M-POOL-POSITION-NEVER-RENEWS
arms.note: a position request through a drifted server invalidates it path by path, one walk of its whole cache each, instead of asking a fresh server

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-SERVER-UNTETHERED
arms.note: the display server is a plain job of its own process group, so a run killed with its driver leaves it running with no owner

arms.name: M-HXML-SPLIT-LAST-SPACE
arms.note: a flag line splits at its LAST space, so `-cp lib -lib heaps` reads as the flag `-cp lib -lib` and the compiler's one classpath is lost

arms.name: M-HXML-QUOTES-KEPT
arms.note: an hxml argument keeps the quotes the compiler drops, so `-cp "src"` names a directory called `"src"`

arms.name: M-COMPILEDIR-PROBE-BLIND
arms.note: the compile-dir probe reads no classpath, so every nested hxml compiles from its own directory even where its classpaths resolve from the config's

arms.name: M-GC-RUN-INHERITS
arms.note: a single haxe spawn inherits the caller's environment untouched, so every typecheck run through `run` pays the default collector again

arms.name: M-GC-DRIVER-INHERITS
arms.note: the parallel driver and every job it starts run in the caller's environment, so the overlapped typechecks run under the default collector

arms.name: M-GC-PENDING-INHERITS
arms.note: a batch started in the background (the facts compiles, the reach probes, the warm servers) runs under the default collector

arms.name: M-GC-INHERITED-OVERRIDDEN
arms.note: our parameters are appended even where the caller's own OCAMLRUNPARAM sets the same one, so a later duplicate overrides the setting the caller chose

arms.name: M-GC-OFF-IGNORED
arms.note: APQ_ORACLE_GC=off is passed to the runtime as a parameter named off instead of leaving the collector alone

arms.name: M-GC-EMPTY-DECLARED-OFF
arms.note: an empty APQ_ORACLE_GC (how a test restores an unset variable) turns the tuning off instead of meaning the default

arms.name: M-GC-MEMORY-UNCOUNTED
arms.note: the budget ignores the extra memory a tuned collector's compile holds, so a small machine runs more compiles than it has memory for

arms.name: M-DRIVER-READS-STDIN
arms.note: the jobs are piped to the driver's stdin again, the channel node's spawnSync can stall for good on macOS, so about one runAll in seven hundred at 200 KB hangs the run forever

arms.name: M-DRIVER-UNBOUNDED
arms.note: a wedged parallel driver is waited on forever, so one stopped or stalled driver hangs the whole lint run

arms.name: M-DRIVER-BOUND-IGNORES-ROUNDS
arms.note: the bound is one job's share however many rounds the parallelism splits the jobs into, so an honest run of many jobs on a small machine is killed as wedged

arms.name: M-PENDING-UNBOUNDED
arms.note: await polls a wedged background driver forever: a stopped driver still answers the liveness probe, so the run never ends

arms.name: M-DEFINES-PARSED-DROPPED
arms.note: a probed build names no file it parses, so every module it reads looks compiled by none of the builds

arms.name: M-REACH-STORE-OFF
arms.replace: if (before == null || builds == null || oracles.length > 0) return;
arms.note: the builds an oracle run probed are never stored, so the next run that compiles nothing knows no build

arms.name: M-REACH-KEY-UNCHECKED
arms.find: return now == null || now.key != text(record['key']) ? null : buildsOf(record);
arms.note: a stored record is read under whatever fingerprint the input hashes to now, so builds probed of a source since edited answer for it

arms.name: M-REACH-GENERATION-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a generated hxml whose declared input changed still keys the stored builds, though the oracle run would generate it again

arms.name: M-REACH-LIBRARY-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a stored library source is read back whatever it holds now, so an edited file outside the fingerprint answers as the one the build compiled

arms.name: M-REACH-HASHED-UNCHECKED
arms.find: for (i in 0...oracles.length) if (!OracleCache.readsHashed(key.bases[i], configurations[i].parsed, key.hashed[i])) return;
arms.replace: for (i in 0...oracles.length) if (false && !OracleCache.readsHashed(key.bases[i], configurations[i].parsed, key.hashed[i])) return;
arms.note: a build that parsed a file the fingerprint did not hash — in a dot directory, past the walk's depth, outside every root — is stored, and an edit to that file is answered by the old build

arms.name: M-ORACLE-VERDICT-READS-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a verdict whose compile read a file the fingerprint did not hash is stored, so an edit to that file is answered by the old verdict with no compile

arms.name: M-REACH-RECORD-SHAPE-UNCHECKED
arms.find: return items != null && items.foreach(item -> item is String) ? cast items : null;
arms.replace: return items != null ? cast items : null;
arms.note: a record's string lists are read whatever they hold, so a define that is no string reaches the builds

arms.name: M-NAME-PROOF-ALWAYS-SAME
arms.note: every value-site rewrite reads as confirmed, so a call a build macro of the build configuration re-points is shortened

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-STDIN-DROPPED
arms.note: the text handed in never reaches the compiler, so a rewrite not yet on disk is never asked about

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-STDIN-NOT-INVALIDATED
arms.note: the module the warm compile cached is answered from, so the text handed in is ignored

arms.name: M-POOL-POSITION-STALE-WRITES
arms.note: a path the run wrote within the second the server last read it is answered at its old text, since the server compares modification times in whole seconds

arms.name: M-NAME-PROOF-NO-ASK-AGREES
arms.note: a site no configuration compiles reads as confirmed, so a rewrite nothing typechecked the meaning of is applied

arms.name: M-NAME-PROOF-NO-ANSWER-AGREES
arms.note: a configuration naming no declaration for the original reads as agreement, so a broken display answer confirms any rewrite

arms.name: M-NAME-PROOF-FIRST-PAIR-FOR-EVERY-SITE
arms.note: every site of one round is judged by the first site's two answers, so a rewrite the compiler re-points rides on its neighbour's agreement

arms.name: M-POOL-POSITIONS-FIRST-ASK-TEXT
arms.note: every ask of one round is read at the first ask's text, so the rewritten text is never the one asked about

arms.name: M-POOL-ASKS-NOT-INTERLEAVED
arms.note: one configuration's asks are queued together, so the compile budget's overlapping requests wait at one server while the others idle

arms.name: M-SERVER-PORT-PROBE
arms.note: every port reads as free, so a starter takes a port something else listens on and its client connects to the holder

arms.name: M-SERVER-PROBE-FAILS-CLOSED
arms.note: a probe that cannot run reads as held, so a machine that cannot run it never gets a warm server though the bind would have succeeded

arms.name: M-SERVER-WARM-TRUSTS-ANY-LISTENER
arms.find: if (!isConnectRefusal(res)) return invalidate(port, hxml, cwd, hxml, defines ?? []);
arms.note: any connection a listener takes reads as a server up, so a display oracle is handed back bound to a port something else holds and its retry never runs

arms.name: M-SERVER-DRAWS-NO-FREE-PORT
arms.note: the shared server draws a candidate without asking which port may be taken, so its client connects to whatever holds it before the retry moves on

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-DRAWS-NO-FREE-PORT
arms.note: the display oracle draws a candidate without asking which port may be taken, so its client connects to whatever holds it before the retry moves on

arms.name: M-POOL-DRAWS-NO-FREE-PORT
arms.note: the pool draws a candidate without asking which port may be taken, so its client connects to whatever holds it before the bring-up moves on

arms.name: M-POOL-START-ONE-SHOT
arms.note: a server that exits on its port leaves the configuration with no warm server for the whole run, where every other starter tries another port

arms.name: M-POOL-RESTART-ONE-SHOT

arms.name: M-POOL-START-RETRIES-A-LIVE-SERVER
arms.note: a configuration the server cannot process is searched across every port, each costing the whole readiness poll, though no port mends it

arms.name: M-POOL-RESTART-RETRIES-A-LIVE-SERVER
arms.note: a restart of a configuration the server cannot process is searched across every port, each costing the whole readiness poll, though no port mends it

arms.name: M-POOL-READY-GIVES-UP-ON-A-FAILED-CONNECT
arms.replace: if (reply == null) return false; if (CompilerServer.isServerReply(reply.output)) return true;
arms.note: one client that did not run, as under load, gives up on a server that is coming up, so the configuration has no warm server

arms.name: M-POOL-POLLS-AN-EXITED-SERVER
arms.note: a server that exited is polled to the end of the budget, so each port it lost costs the whole readiness poll before the next is tried

arms.name: M-NAME-PROOF-RAW-POSITIONS
arms.find: if (was.byLine || now.byLine || was.file != now.file || !FileIdentity.same(was.file, file)) return samePosition(was, now);
arms.note: the two answers are compared raw, so a target declared in the edited file is declined whenever an import is inserted above it

arms.name: M-NAME-PROOF-EVERY-ANSWER-CARRIED
arms.find: if (was.byLine || now.byLine || was.file != now.file || !FileIdentity.same(was.file, file)) return samePosition(was, now);
arms.note: an answer in another file, or by whole lines, is carried through the edited file's rewrite as if it stood there, so a target elsewhere reads as moved and the rewrite is declined

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-NO-PLAIN-RETRY

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-DECISIVE-DIAGNOSTICS-ONLY

arms.name: M-DEFINE-READS-NONE
arms.note: no source reads a define, so a build whose #if names the facts hook's define is answered from the compile that set it

arms.name: M-DEFINE-READS-LITERAL-ANYWHERE
arms.find: ? word != ALL_DEFINES && wholeLiteral(source, literal, at, word.length) && readerBefore(source, at)

arms.name: M-DEFINE-READS-ALL-DEFINES-DECLARED

arms.name: M-RIDDEN-KEEPS-HOOK-LOADS

arms.name: M-RIDDEN-SHADOW-UNCHECKED
arms.find: return held != null && held == text ? candidate : null;
arms.note: a project module the hook shadows is taken for the hook's copy whatever its text, so the build the shared compile typed is not the project's

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-BUILD-UNGUARDED
arms.note: a build compiled while the tree changed is filed under the fingerprint taken before, so once the tree is back at that content it answers for a tree it may never have read
